contents.name: Définition 1.3.1 (t-catégorie: shift-closed strictly full subcategories, orthogonality, decomposition triangle; heart)
Exemples 1.3.2 (the natural t-structure on D(𝒜) by cohomological support; translation and opposite t-structures)
Proposition 1.3.3 (adjunction of τ≤n and τ≥n to the inclusions of the aisles; essential uniqueness of the decomposition triangle)
1.3.4 (each aisle is the orthogonal of the other; both aisles are stable under extensions and finite direct sums)
Proposition 1.3.5 (two-sided truncation τ_[a,b] and the canonical isomorphisms τ≤b τ≥a)
Théorème 1.3.6 (heart is an admissible abelian subcategory stable under extensions; H⁰ = τ≥0 τ≤0 is a cohomological functor, with long exact cohomology sequence)
contents.reason: The heart's abelianness and the long exact t-cohomology sequence are not used by this pair: the splitting lemma's interior-degree comparison is proved from additivity and concentration, so importing Théorème 1.3.6 would add an unused heavy prerequisite.

contents.name: Proposition 1.3.7 (for a nondegenerate t-structure the functors H* are conservative and detect membership in each aisle)
contents.reason: This pair needs amplitude detection only for bounded t-structures, which is proved locally (both directions) without nondegeneracy; the printed conservativity theorem's extra generality is not consumed here.

contents.name: 1.3.8–1.3.9 (converse problem: which abelian subcategories occur as hearts of a t-category)
contents.reason: The heart reconstruction problem is not part of the abstract splitting route, and no item of this pair asserts or uses the heart's abelianness or a reconstruction theorem.

contents.name: Théorème 5.4.10 (relative hard Lefschetz for a pure perverse sheaf under a projective morphism)
contents.reason: This is the geometric relative hard Lefschetz theorem; it is consumed by that page's relative perverse splitting theorem, not by the abstract t-structure splitting proved in this pair.

contents.name: Lemmes 5.4.11–5.4.13 (the universal-hyperplane comparison, the projective-bundle formula and the local perverse-cohomology computation used to prove 5.4.10)
contents.reason: These are the local geometric components of the printed proof of 5.4.10 and belong with that theorem on the projective perverse page; the abstract splitting lemma uses none of them.

contents.name: Proposition (1.2) (X ∈ D^b(𝒜) splits as ⊕ H^i(X)[−i] if and only if the spectral sequence of every cohomological functor degenerates)
Remarque (1.4) (it suffices to test the degeneration criterion on functors Hom(A,−) or Hom(−,A))
contents.reason: The scaffold proof verifies the splitting directly by a finite amplitude induction inside a bounded t-structure and never runs the spectral-sequence degeneration criterion, so this reduction is not used.

contents.name: Théorème (1.5) (a degree-two endomorphism u with H^{−i}(u^i) an isomorphism forces X ≅ ⊕ H^i(X)[−i] in D^b(𝒜))
(1.6)–(1.7) (the primitive pieces and the isomorphisms ⊕ u^k : ⊕ PH^{n−i−2k} → H^{n−i} used in the proof of (1.5))
Remarque (1.8) (in general no splitting can be chosen to intertwine u with the shifted sum of the H^i(u) maps)
contents.reason: The scaffolded splitting lemma explicitly makes no canonicity assertion; the remark's warning concerns a stronger statement that this pair deliberately does not make.

contents.name: Remarque (1.9) (the degree-s variant with cohomology supported in the multiples of s)
contents.reason: Only the degree-two two-step Lefschetz operator is needed for the consumers of this page; the general degree-s variant is not used by any scaffolded item.

contents.name: Remarque (1.10) (the formal family version when the direct sum of the X_i does not exist in D^b(𝒜))
contents.reason: The scaffolded statements concern a single bounded object and a finite direct sum; no infinite family and no formal direct-sum device is required.

contents.name: Théorème (1.11) and Corollaire (1.12) (decomposition along orthogonal idempotents; finite direct sums of the X_i)
contents.reason: Idempotent decomposition theorems and the finite-sum refinement are not used: the amplitude induction produces its direct sum from the split triangle and the t-structure alone.

contents.name: Remarque (1.13) (the unique splitting that intertwines orthogonal idempotents)
contents.reason: This sharpening of the splitting's canonicity is outside the scope of the abstract lemma, which asserts existence of a splitting only and explicitly disclaims canonicity.

contents.name: §2 (the Lefschetz condition for a sheaf and Proposition (2.1))
contents.reason: The geometric Lefschetz-condition applications belong to the perverse-sheaf pages of this run; this pair needs only the algebraic criterion of §1.
